_rationale: docs/QUALITY-CONTRACT.md. Notes below hold no measured status on purpose: for status run `python tools/gate/gate.py run --project .`

app._note: unused; kept in the shape the gate expects so a future served component has somewhere to go

build._note: the only subproject with an installable manifest; tools/ has none and imports stdlib only

unit.cmd: python -m pytest tests/ -q && python tools/gate/gate.py selftest && python tools/review/panel.py selftest && cd intent-control-plane && uv run pytest -q
unit._note: every automated-test entrypoint in the repo, including both oracles' own selftests
unit._timeout_note: Raised 300 -> 900 on 2026-07-31 with the measurement rather than by feel. The 300s budget was set when the root suite was 70 tests in about 47s. It is now 331 tests in 182s, and this domain chains FOUR commands: the root suite, the gate selftest, the panel selftest, and the intent-control-plane suite at about 50s. Total is roughly 250s on an idle machine and it timed out at 300s three times on 2026-07-31 under concurrent load, which produced a FAIL that named no failing test and sent two diagnoses down the wrong path. The honest alternative is splitting this into unit and subproject domains so a slow subproject cannot mask a fast regression; that is a contract shape change and is deferred to a ticket rather than done inside a timeout bump. Falsifier: if the suite passes 600s this number is hiding growth again and the split is overdue.

types.cmd: python -m compileall -q -x "\\.venv|venv" . && cd intent-control-plane && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy
types._note: compileall is the documented fallback where no root lint config exists; ruff and mypy are configured inside intent-control-plane

e2e.na_reason: claude-setup serves no application of its own. tools/e2e/flow.py and tools/browser/cdp.py drive other repositories' running UIs from whichever contract is being evaluated; every .html in this tree is a static export, not a route. See docs/QUALITY-CONTRACT.md.

a11y_ux.na_reason: Reads the e2e report at a stricter threshold, and there is no e2e report because there is no served app. If any part of this repo grows a UI, both this and e2e move to a real cmd rather than staying NA by default.

security._note: known blind spot is documented beside the patterns in gate.py, not here

docs._note: TODO.md is in the list because this repo describes changes there and in docs/analysis/, not in CHANGELOG.md

pipeline._note: local-green and CI-green have to be about the same checks

review._note: artifact is matched by commit sha, not by tree, so one written against a dirty tree stays current for that commit
review._waiver_history: A waiver until 2026-08-02 was REMOVED on 2026-08-06, expired rather than renewed, because its reason had ended. It waived exactly one thing: that the review domain refuses to certify a dirty tree, and the tree then carried uncommitted work the waiver's author did not own. That work is now committed, so the condition is gone. Its own text set the exit: 'Short expiry on purpose: committing the tree should clear it, not renew it.' Confirmed by running the command it named rather than trusting it: python tools/review/panel.py run --project . -> 'VERDICT: PASS (0 high, 0 medium, 0 low)', 618 added lines across 10 files, 32 pattern checks, 5 personas. Following the prior_art precedent in this file: a waiver ends when its reason does, and the history is recorded rather than deleted. The prior text is preserved below so the two defects it documented (sql-concat needing SQL structure, added_lines dropping stale positions) are not lost with it. PRIOR REASON: Replaces the 2026-08-12 waiver, whose stated reason was measurably WRONG and is recorded here rather than deleted. It said all 5 HIGHs were matches against comments and docstrings. Three were prose (an English 'Delete ... + their selftest' in two docs/prior-art JSON records and a print() of a delete result), and two were REAL shell=True code on lines this branch added and then deleted, reported against line numbers now occupied by the comment recording that deletion. Comments were never the mechanism. Both defects are now fixed in the oracle rather than waived: sql-concat requires SQL structure (FROM/INTO/SET) as well as a concatenation, and added_lines drops any line the tree no longer contains at the position it claims. tests/test_panel_sql_concat.py and tests/test_panel_stale_lines.py pin both, 20 cases; mutate.py --spec panel is 10 of 10 caught. The panel now returns 0 high. WHAT IS STILL WAIVED is only this: the review domain refuses to certify a dirty tree ('_note' above), and this tree carries uncommitted work that is not mine to commit. Nothing about the code is being excused. CONFIRM BY RUNNING, do not trust this sentence: python tools/review/panel.py run --project . -- expected 'VERDICT: PASS  (0 high'. If that reports any high finding, this waiver is FALSE and must be revoked. Short expiry on purpose: committing the tree should clear it, not renew it.

perf.na_reason: No performance budget is declared for claude-setup, which serves no application and has no latency to bound. Corrected 2026-08-08: the previous wording went further and said nobody had set a number to measure against anywhere in the tree, and that is false. The unit domain's own _timeout_note, written 2026-07-31 and so six days after this reason, sets a 900s budget with an explicit falsifier at 600s. Separately, intent-control-plane/repo_health.py enforces FILE_BUDGET, FUNC_BUDGET and CLASS_BUDGET, a maintainability budget rather than a perf one, and it is referenced by no pyproject script, by gate.py, or by CI, so it runs nowhere. The Lighthouse and p95-without-a-threshold halves of the original claim were re-checked by grep and still hold. N/A is retained because a duration budget on the gate's own run is not what this domain measures, but the enabling half landed today: gate runs now record duration_seconds and domain_seconds, so the unit falsifier is evaluable for the first time. The 8571 rows before that carry no duration at all. Whether that becomes a real perf domain is a contract shape decision and belongs to the operator, with the evidence in docs/analysis/2026-08-08-na-domains-rechecked.md.

codemap._note: every tracked directory states a purpose, and docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md matches the tree
codemap._waiver_history: A waiver until 2026-08-06 was added and REMOVED the same hour, unexpired. It excused 5 registry rows naming research-papers/docs-shoval subdirectories that another session had staged for deletion, and its stated reason was that removing the rows would finish half of somebody else's uncommitted change. Then `python tools/map/codemap.py write` was run to register a new directory and it removed those 5 rows as a side effect, which is exactly what the waiver said not to do. The pre-run backup diff reported no change to dir-purpose.txt and was wrong; `git diff` shows 5 deletions and 1 insertion. Recording the sequence rather than the outcome, because the outcome (map clean) looks identical whether the rows were removed deliberately or by a regeneration nobody inspected. Restore with `git checkout docs/dir-purpose.txt` and re-add the tools/antigravity row if the deletion is reverted upstream.

docmap._note: Every tracked markdown file has a derivable or declared lifecycle status, and docs/DOCMAP.md matches what the documents imply. Declared 2026-07-31, six days after the tool was written: docmap ran clean the whole time and NOTHING enforced it, which is the same shape as a hook that cannot fire. A hand edit to DOCMAP.md reads as drift and fails, exactly as CODEBASE-MAP.md does, because both are generated. The residue that cannot be derived lives in docs/doc-status.txt, currently 44 rows against a stated ceiling of 37; growth past that means the derivation rules are wrong rather than that the registry should grow.

prior_art._note: every component over 300 lines of Python carries an unexpired record naming what else could do its job
prior_art._waiver_history: A waiver until 2026-08-01 was added on 2026-07-31 and REMOVED the same day, unexpired, because the thing it excused was done rather than waited out. Its reason was correct when written: commit 8a4217b brought syndication-engine (549 lines), whatsapp-query (1120) and tools/intent (1016) fully into tracking with no prior-art records, and inventing three records to clear a red domain would have fabricated the evidence this domain exists to demand. All three now exist with 7, 8 and 7 fetched-and-cited alternatives and counterarguments that argue against keeping our version. Recorded here rather than deleted, because L-2026-07-31-a is a waiver renewed twice on a reason nobody executed, and the counter-practice worth keeping is that a waiver ends when its reason does.

rules._note: the global rules loaded into every session are deployed AND intact. Added 2026-08-04 after twelve of them were found at roughly a tenth of their original size, having been overwritten by commit 2bb97a8 which synced a degraded live tree back over the good repo copy and removed 986 lines. Nothing in the repo could see it: skills_sync.py covers dot-claude/skills and never mentioned rules. The shrink half of this check is the part that matters, because a byte count is the only signal left once the content is gone.

skills._note: dot-claude/skills and ~/.claude/skills agree. The checker already existed and already returned 1 on drift; what was missing was anything that ran it, so a real oracle reported problems into a terminal nobody gated on. Added 2026-08-05. The count it enforces was corrected the same day: a byte hash counted a CRLF live file and an LF repo file as drift, which inflated 55 to include 4 character-identical pairs. Those now report under LINE ENDINGS ONLY and do not fail, because no decision exists for a file whose characters match.

waived.reason: waived until 2026-08-16, restated 2026-08-12 at DRIFT: 8, down from 16 because the 2026-08-12 dir-organization merge (PR #63) absorbed the dot-agents bucket and this session committed repo-compare, the one skill that existed only live. What remains is two problems, both needing a human. (a) 4 COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED: prod-deploy-rules, jira-task-draft, writing-great-skills, jira-read; deploying them writes the live ~/.claude tree and stays the operator's call, unchanged from the prior waiver. (b) 4 SAME NAME DIFFERENT BYTES forks: case-ledger-post (repo 19565b, live 25365b), grill-me (635b vs 1261b), shoval-voice-draft (27401b vs 10935b), youtube-distill (12545b vs 8205b). Byte size does not order recency (grill-me proves it: repo is smaller and AHEAD), so overwriting either side risks destroying newer work; each fork needs the human who made the live edit. PRIOR REASON, kept because its diagnosis of the fork class still holds: waived until 2026-08-12, restated 2026-08-10 at DRIFT: 16, up one from the 15 recorded on 2026-08-09. The increase is not a regression in anything this repository did. A skill named case-ledger-post changed IN THE LIVE TREE at 2026-08-10 12:13 local, during a session that did not write it, taking that entry from agreeing to SAME NAME DIFFERENT BYTES (repo 19565b, live 25365b). Two clones of this repository run in parallel on this machine and the live ~/.claude tree is shared between them, so a live-side edit arriving mid-session is expected rather than surprising. It is left undecided on purpose: a byte count orders files by size and says nothing about which is current, and overwriting either side would destroy whoever's work is newer. Resolving it needs a human who knows what changed at 12:13. The other 15 are unchanged and are still three different problems. (a) 4 COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED, so no session can invoke prod-deploy-rules, jira-task-draft, writing-great-skills or jira-read; deploying them is a live-tree change and the operator's. (b) 8 DEPLOYED BUT NOT COMMITTED, every one tracked under dot-agents/skills, a third tree skills_sync does not read at all, so this bucket measures the oracle as much as the repository and closing it means deciding the three-tree question AGENTS.md records as open. (c) 3 genuine forks: shoval-voice-draft (repo 27401b, live 10935b), youtube-distill (12545b against 8205b), and grill-me, where live is larger yet the repo is AHEAD because 3df7704 rewrote it into a terse brief while live still holds the older protocol, which is the clearest available proof that size does not order recency. Three skills keep disable-model-invocation on purpose and are not drift: skillmap and wayfinder carry it in BOTH trees, making it a deployed decision, and writing-great-skills is undeployed so it sits in bucket (a). Expiry unchanged at 2026-08-12. The waiver got one item larger, not one day longer.

pointers._note: hooks and skills that name a path which does not resolve. Same shape as the skills row: a real checker that CI never invoked. Measured 2026-08-05 it exits 0 at fail-on=high while carrying 271 distinct absent paths, headed by ~/.claude/bin/work-item.sh at 40 references, so this row gates the high-severity class only and the long tail stays visible without blocking. No waiver, because it passes today.
pointers.scope_note: Runs with --include-live from 2026-08-07. Without it the scan read the committed dot-claude/settings.json and never ~/.claude/settings.json, so it audited a payload copy instead of the file that runs. That is not a weaker check, it is a check of a different file under the same name: the live settings had been wiring a PostToolUse hook at tools/intent/spawn_log.py, which did not exist, failing on every agent spawn, while this domain reported PASS. The payload copy has no PostToolUse section at all, so the broken hook was outside the file being read rather than merely missed. On a runner there is no live settings and the scan says so in as many words instead of passing quietly.
